_wiring: Plaits OUT -> audio interface input 1, AUX -> input 2 (line level, gain at minimum). oC (FX Rig app, USB to the Mac): A -> passive mult (or stackable cable) -> V/OCT and LEVEL; jack B -> LEVEL instead of the mult for the tour (role level); jack G -> TRIGGER when an experiment asks for it; C -> MODEL (re-patch it after flashing: MODEL is the update input); D -> HARMONICS; jack H -> FM (role debug: the commands of the rig firmware, see plaits/rig/rig.h); audio interface output 2 (as the Mac numbers them; the user patched the jack it reaches) -> MODEL (the updates, from the rig firmware's updater; MODEL CV from the oC is then unused) instead of oC jack C; E -> TIMBRE; F -> MORPH. Knobs: FREQUENCY at about 9 o'clock, HARMONICS at 12 o'clock, TIMBRE fully counterclockwise, MORPH at about 11 o'clock (a clean pitch for the classic waveforms); TIMBRE and MORPH attenuverters fully clockwise, FM attenuverter centered.

virtual._: The virtual module: plaits-sim-rig, with a typical ADC (typical: its gain error, -2.7% in STM32F373's datasheet, which --hw can replace), calibrated as at the factory (the original firmware's V/OCT calibration, with exact 1V and 3V, which also measures the 0V readings of the other inputs), then with the knobs as in _wiring. TRIGGER is unplugged until an experiment asks for it.

_oc: FX Rig's channels (A-H in its software). On the oC used for this rig, the two rows of jacks are swapped against them: the jack labelled A is channel E, B is F, C is G, D is H, E is A, F is B, G is C, H is D (measured 2026-10-12). The wiring above uses the jack labels.
